definitions.equation: A mathematical statement that two expressions are equal.
definitions.equality: The relationship indicating that two expressions have the same value.
definitions.solution: A value of a variable that makes an equation true.
definitions.solution set: The complete set of values satisfying an equation or system.
definitions.inverse operation: An operation that undoes another, such as division undoing multiplication.
definitions.equivalent equation: Equations that have exactly the same solutions in the specified domain.
definitions.identity: An equation true for every permitted value of its variable.
definitions.contradiction: An equation that has no solution because it implies a false statement, such as 0=5.
definitions.literal equation: An equation involving two or more symbols, solved for one named symbol.
definitions.formula: A rule expressing the relationship among quantities using mathematical symbols.
definitions.proportion: An equation stating that two ratios are equal.
definitions.ratio: A comparison of two quantities by division, with consistent units.
definitions.direct variation: A relationship y=kx for a constant k, so y/x=k when x is nonzero.
definitions.constant of proportionality: The constant k in a direct variation or other proportional equation.
definitions.percent equation: An equation relating a part, base, and percent, often part=rate×base.
definitions.rate: A comparison of change in one quantity per unit change in another.
definitions.distance: How far an object travels; in constant-speed motion distance=rate×time.
definitions.mixture: A model balancing the amounts or concentrations of combined materials.
definitions.simple interest: Interest calculated on the original principal only: I=Prt for compatible units.
definitions.domain: The set of allowed input values in a relation, function, or expression.
definitions.constraint: A restriction a solution must obey, including values prohibited by denominators.
definitions.verification: Testing a candidate in the original equation or context to confirm it is valid.
